data.gender_notes: Ivansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ivansh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Iva' which means 'God' and 'Ansh' which means 'Form'. The name Ivansh signifies the presence of Lord Shiva in a child. This name is believed to bring immense power, protection, and blessings to the child. The name Ivansh carries the meaning “Lord Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ivansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The elephant-headed god, Lord Ganesha, is a deity widely revered and honored in the Hindu pantheon. He is the god of wisdom, knowledge, new beginnings, and is believed to remove obstacles and bring success.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ganesha is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Gana' meaning 'Group' and 'Is' meaning 'Lord'. It represents the supreme lord of all groups, symbols of unity and collective consciousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ivansh: God Shiva's grace and protection embodied. The name is derived from 'Ishana' (God) and 'Vansh' (lineage or progeny), symbolizing the divine blessings bestowed upon one's lineage.

historical_references.reference: Ivansh was a legendary king of the Solar Dynasty, also known as the Ikshvaku Dynasty, according to Hindu mythology. He was the great-grandson of Rama, the hero of the epic Ramayana. Ivansh ruled Hastinapur, the ancient capital city of the Kuru dynasty, around the 10th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology, Solar Dynasty, Ikshvaku Dynasty, legendary king, Rama's great-grandson, Hastinapur, ancient capital city of the Kuru dynasty

historical_references.reference: Ivansh is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the father of Uttara, the wife of Arjuna. She was born to Ivansh and his wife, Prabha, and was later raised by King Janamejaya. Ivansh's time is estimated to be around the 3rd century BCE.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata, ancient Indian epic, father of Uttara, wife of Arjuna, born to Ivansh and Prabha, raised by Janamejaya
